blocks.text: A chemistry laboratory is a chemist's workshop: a place where a student is trained to observe the physical and chemical characteristics of substances by following definite procedures. Before starting laboratory work a student should become familiar with the layout of the laboratory and the various fittings provided on the laboratory table and the side shelves.

items: Students are expected to conduct themselves in a responsible manner at all times in the lab.
Do not work alone in the lab; experiments are performed in the presence of the lab instructor and other laboratory staff.
Always wear a lab coat and safety goggles while working; tie up scarves and hair before starting work.
Determine the potential hazards of any equipment or experiment before beginning any work, and observe the appropriate safety precautions at all costs.
No crowding in the lab: stick to your work place at a safe distance from each other.
Do not bring food into the lab; never taste or smell any compound or gas.
Report any accident or breakage of glassware to the in-charge of the laboratory immediately.
If you cannot handle an instrument or piece of equipment properly, seek help from the instructor.
Do not pour chemicals down the drains and do not use the sewer for chemical waste disposal.
Follow the warning signs displayed in the lab.
